intro: A state transition can be accepted or rejected without changing the number of events in a trace. Keeping both the balance and an acceptance flag makes rejected operations visible.
task: Trace account balance while rejecting withdrawals that exceed available funds.
requirements: initial is integer 0..1e9; changes are signed integers within +/-1e9. Apply each change only when resulting balance is nonnegative. Return balances after every attempt and accepted booleans; positive balances may grow beyond 1e9.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Test the tentative balance before committing the update.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Record a balance after a rejected attempt too, so outputs remain aligned with changes.

explanation: A state transition can be accepted or rejected without changing the number of events in a trace. Keeping both the balance and an acceptance flag makes rejected operations visible.
The invariant is nonnegative balance after every attempt. Rejecting an overdraft must preserve the previous balance rather than clipping it to zero or allowing a later deposit to hide the error.
